parts.title: Questions people ask first
parts.summary: The things a new owner searches for, answered from the sections above.

sections.title: How often should I dump the black tank?

blocks.html: When it is about two thirds full, and never by leaving the valve open at a full-hookup site. Leaving it open lets the liquid drain away and the solids stay, which is how a tank becomes a pile. The manual is explicit that the valve stays closed: "keep the black-water holding tank gate valve closed at all times, except when dumping".

Precharge it afterwards. A tank that starts dry is a tank that starts with a problem: "After dumping, always precharge your tank before using it again." The same manual gives the recipe as one to two quarts in the bowl, then a flush that puts at least two gallons into the tank.
Dump black first, then grey. The grey water rinses the hose, and the order is in the manual: "Drain the black-water tank first before draining the grey"

sections.title: Do I need a water pressure regulator?

blocks.html: Yes, on city water. Campground supply pressure varies and the plumbing in an RV is built for less than a house system. The manual states the threshold: "NOTE: If city water pressure is more than 60 psi, Tiffin Motor Homes recommends to use a water pressure regulator." It goes on the tap end of your drinking-water hose, not inside the compartment.

sections.title: How long do RV tires last?

blocks.html: The manufacturers disagree, and anybody who tells you there is one answer is repeating a rule nobody publishes. Goodyear's service bulletin says "6 years" from the date of manufacture. Michelin says inspect from five years and replace by ten. NHTSA describes manufacturer practice as six to ten.
The "5-7-10 rule" is not an RVIA or NHTSA rule. It circulates widely and traces to no published document from either body. Tire age is decided by the maker of your tire, not by a rule of thumb.
Age is read from the DOT code on the sidewall, not from tread depth. A tire with plenty of tread and a 2016 date code is a ten-year-old tire.

sections.title: What should I do on the very first day?

blocks.html: Level first, before the slide-outs move and before an absorption fridge runs. Fill the water heater before it is switched on. Keep the electrical load off while the shore cord goes in. The twelve items at the top of this page are the ones that cost money if they are got wrong, and each of them is a minute of work.
